title: Joining the Chicago musicians' union; the traveling transfer
summary: Garland resists, then joins the union after the walking delegate pressures the club; he shows a transfer card for the Local 6 move to San Francisco.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: No, no, no, no, no. There wasn't no big girls there, no. Dancing? Dancing and entertaining. Billy Bottoms had the same thing across the way. Then Billy Bottoms, they all got crazy about the jazz band. I could get a job all around. The first time I went to the union, all right, here come the walking delegate now. The walking delegate come up, talking about, I have to join the union. I said, you crazy. I ain't stood about no union. You ain't going to mess me up. You all need to join the union so you can take me off this job or take me out of. Have your favorites and I'll be around you and won't have no job. You got to join the job everybody, you know. All them waiters is union, you see? I'll argue with them. I said, come back again. I said, well, all right. We'll give you another week. This week you're going to join the union or you can come out of here. They told Shaw that he was going to pull all the waiters out. I said, Mr. Shaw, I said, golly, come here tomorrow and I ain't going to meet you. I don't know what he's going to want me for. I goes over there and he gives me a check. He's going out of the union. I said, for what? He said, he got to join the union. I said, all right, take this check. Go down up here for the boys. I went down and I won't show you. I can show you right now. I think I got the proof right here. I got out of the union. We joined the union. Everything was all right. So, I've been in the union ever since. What is it? Now, this is something there I should have this. That's what you call a traveling transfer. A transfer. When I went to Frisco with King Oliver, who went to number six, was playing 피cola. That was in 1920. That's your transfer. Now that'll tell you when I read it out. You and you did.
Yes. I'm trying to. Pull that loose. I'm not tearing it. You see, Copeland was second time.
It says July 1st, 1921. Well, that's when I got that transfer. Oh.
This is later. Oh, well, it was just I've been in the years. July 1st, 1921.
Well, you've been on the West Coast. I didn't want to know.

That's when, that's one, that's a transfer when I left, you see. We left in 20. Uh-huh. And come to Frisco, that's when I want. Now you look, you see number six. You can see the local number six, that's in Frisco. Yes. Well, how long did you stay in Chicago?
